## The problem

A **packaged** Papercusp install today pays two serial waits: the app download,
then a first-boot **dogfood join** that is genuinely heavy:

- **Git.** `bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts` clones `github.com/Papercusp/papercup` —
  a **~5 GB tree + ~6.2 GB `.git` + 27 submodules** (the module header states the
  repo is "far too large to bundle"; submodules init best-effort in the background
  after the pot appears).
- **Substrate.** The shared-pot join re-keys the joined harnesses onto the owner's
  federation topic and the read-merge (`boot.ts` → `mergeAdmittedLogs`) replays
  **every admitted peer's per-peer Hypercore log from block 0** into PG. Cold, over
  the network, capped at 50k ops/author.

We *want* to keep paying the join — it is the best possible test of the real
shared-pot join procedure ("the app can't work if this part doesn't work"). We
just don't want the user to **wait for the cold, full-history transfer** when the
bytes could have shipped in the installer.

## The insight — seed the BYTES, let the join bootstrap the TRUST

Both stores are **seed-then-catch-up native**. A *seed* pre-positions bytes at a
known checkpoint; the **unmodified** join then transfers only the delta on top:

| Store | Native checkpoint | Post-seed delta transfer | Self-verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hypercore/corestore | a copy of the corestore with each author core at length `N` | replication fetches only blocks `> N` (`core.update()` → download tail) | per-block **merkle** proof + author **signature** on open |
| Git | a `git bundle` | `clone --bundle-uri` then `fetch` = only new objects | git object **hashes** (content-addressed) |

**The mantra (D-001): the seed bootstraps bytes; the live join bootstraps trust.**
A seed is *untrusted cache*. Every store re-verifies natively, and **admission stays
the sole trust/keys path** — the join procedure is not modified, so the dogfood keeps
exercising the real thing end-to-end (invite → owner announce → admission → epoch
keys → live tail). If a seed is absent, stale, corrupt, or fails verification, the
system degrades to today's cold path (D-007).

> **Update (2026-07 — WI-3232 "Full pot, plaintext seed"): admission is no longer
> the ONLY keys path.** For alpha (no users yet, owner-authorised), the installer
> can ship the pot **epoch key readable inside the seed** as `epoch-keys.json`
> (emitted by `cut-seed-cli --emit-epoch-key`). `bundled-epoch-key-provider.ts`
> resolves that key **offline**, so a FRESH packaged install decrypts the seed —
> both the encrypted git bundles and the epoch-encrypted corestore content
> (`POT_REKEY` default-ON) — with **no federation join / admission at all**. This
> is wired live in `bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts` via `epoch-key-provider-chain.ts`,
> which tries the FEDERATED member provider first (PG-wrapped `hive_epoch_keys`,
> holds all granted epochs `[0..cur]`, stays correct after a re-key) and falls back
> to the bundled provider — so an online member is unchanged while a cold install
> self-admits. It remains fail-closed: a missing/wrong bundled key throws
> `EpochKeyUnavailableError` and the op defers exactly as before. The design below
> (admission-delivered `SeedKeyRef.via: "seed-key-op"` / epoch-key, D-004) is the
> **v1 federated** key path and still holds for a real multi-member pot; the
> bundled path is the additive alpha self-admit layer on the SAME `EpochKeyProvider`
> seam. Runbook: the seed-bundle runbook + WI-3232.

This is **not** a revival of `_retired/snapshot-system/` (D-006). That was a
monolithic-era harness-tarball *distribution* mechanism whose jobs were re-homed to
blueprints (distribution), git+PG (backup), and `InstanceSpec` (reproducible clone).
A seed-bundle is a different primitive: **a checkpoint of a REPLICATED store,
restored before that store's native catch-up protocol runs.** `InstanceSpec` boots a
*fresh* instance from `(blueprintRef, repoSha, deploymentConfig, genome)`; a seed
carries *existing replicated content* to skip a cold transfer. A seed-ref may later
become an optional `InstanceSpec` field, but the two are orthogonal today.

## Scope — both halves of the dogfood (D-002)

The owner's dogfood is **not just what is in git** — it is also **what is shared over
the pot**: plans, work items, features, issues, coordination, pot settings, pot
members. Those live in the **federated substrate** (per-peer Hypercore logs →
PG projections), so the **corestore seed carries them** and the **git seed carries the
code**. A complete seed = `{ git bundle set, corestore copy, manifest }`.

## Architecture

### Generic core: `libs/generic/seed-bundle` (D-006, repo generic-first convention)

A domain-free library behind a `configure*()` seam (BORROWABLE; `npm run
gen:borrowable`). It owns the manifest, packing/unpacking, hashing/verification, and
a **provider registry** — but knows nothing about git or Hypercore. The substrate
specifics live in **providers colocated with their substrates**.

```ts
// libs/generic/seed-bundle — the generic contract
export interface SeedManifest {
  seedFormatVersion: number;          // bump on breaking shape change
  hiveId: string;                     // which pot this seed reconstitutes
  cutAtEpoch: number;                 // pot epoch at cut time (see Q-4)
  cutHlc: string;                     // HLC stamp of the cut (ordering anchor)
  cutTs: number;                      // wall-clock ms, provenance only
  stores: SeedStoreEntry[];
}

export interface SeedStoreEntry {
  kind: string;                       // provider id, e.g. "corestore" | "git"
  hash: string;                       // content hash of the payload (verify gate)
  sizeBytes: number;
  source: SeedSource;                 // WHERE the payload bytes come from
  encryption?: SeedEncryptionEnvelope;// present ⇒ payload is ciphertext at rest
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;     // provider-specific (e.g. per-core lengths)
}

// Open-ended so v2 can CDN/swarm-fetch WITHOUT a schema change (D-003).
export type SeedSource =
  | { type: "resource"; path: string }          // v1: a Tauri bundled resource
  | { type: "url"; url: string; bytes: number }  // v2: resumable CDN blob
  | { type: "swarm"; topic: string };            // v3: peer-fetched

export interface SeedEncryptionEnvelope {
  scheme: string;                     // e.g. "xchacha20poly1305"
  keyRef: SeedKeyRef;                 // HOW the decrypt key is obtained
  nonce?: string;
}
// The key is NEVER in the installer. It is delivered by the live join.
export type SeedKeyRef =
  | { via: "epoch"; hiveId: string; epoch: number }   // unwrap from hive_epoch_keys
  | { via: "seed-key-op"; hiveId: string };            // a dedicated admission content-op

export interface SeedProvider {
  kind: string;
  /** Produce a self-verifying checkpoint of the live store (build/release time). */
  cut(ctx: SeedCutContext): Promise<SeedStoreEntry & { payload: SeedPayload }>;
  /** Cheap integrity check BEFORE restore (hash + shape). Never trusts blindly. */
  verify(entry: SeedStoreEntry, payload: SeedPayload): Promise<VerifyResult>;
  /** Drop the checkpoint into place so the store's NATIVE catch-up resumes from it. */
  restore(entry: SeedStoreEntry, payload: SeedPayload, ctx: SeedRestoreContext): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Provider 1 — corestore (colocated in `sync/hyperbee/`)

Carries the **federated pot state**. From `corestore.ts`, a harness's substrate is a
plain directory tree at `<workspaceRoot>/.papercusp/<harness>/hyperbee/` (Hypercore
storage: each author's signed append-only log, `peer-log.ts`).

- **cut** = a consistent copy of that directory with each author core at its current
  length. Record per-core lengths in `entry.meta`. (The sibling `hyperbee-scoped/`
  store is per-connection-served and MUST NOT be seeded — it is never `.replicate()`d;
  seeding it would leak scoped cores. Corestore provider seeds `hyperbee/` only.)
- **restore** = drop the tree into the same path **before `bootHarnessSubstrate`
  opens the store**. Boot then opens the seeded cores; the read-merge replays the
  *local* seeded ops into PG (rebuilding projections — D-005, no PG dump) and swarm
  replication fetches only blocks past the seeded length.
- **verify** = Hypercore's own merkle + author-signature on open. A tampered/truncated
  core fails to open → fall back to cold.

**Why this is safe against a malicious seed:** every op in a seeded core is
author-signed and the core is merkle-verified; admission independently decides *which*
author logs are admitted. A seed cannot inject an op the author didn't sign, nor admit
an unadmitted author.

### Provider 2 — git (colocated near `clone-github.ts` / `git-sync`)

- **cut** = a `git bundle` set: the superproject + all 27 submodules (each bundle is a
  content-addressed pack).
- **restore** = `git clone --bundle-uri` (or clone-from-bundle then set remote), point
  `origin` at `github.com/Papercusp/papercup`, wire submodule bundles, then a normal
  `fetch` pulls only the delta. Auth continues to flow through the user's `gh`
  credential helper exactly as `clone-github.ts` documents (no token in our process).
- **verify** = git verifies pack object hashes on index; `git fsck` optional.

## Restore-before-join state machine

```
FRESH INSTALL
   │
   ├─ seed present & manifest parses? ──no──┐
   │            │yes                          │
   ▼                                          │
 VERIFY each store entry (hash/shape) ──fail──┤
   │ pass                                      │
   ▼                                           │
 RESTORE git seed → checkout on disk           │
 RESTORE corestore seed → .papercusp/<h>/hyperbee/
   │ (git seed still CIPHERTEXT until key)      │
   ▼                                           │
 ── UNMODIFIED JOIN ─────────────────────────► │
   invite subscribe → owner announce →         │
   ADMISSION → epoch keys arrive               │
   │                                           │
   ├─ decrypt git seed with admission key      │
   ├─ substrate boot: local replay → PG,       │
   │  swarm replication fetches DELTA blocks    │
   └─ git fetch pulls DELTA objects             │
   │                                            │
   ▼                                            ▼
 USABLE POT (delta-only)              COLD PATH (today's full clone
                                        + cold read-merge) ── identical end state
```

Any restore failure at any point drops to the **cold path** (right column). A
`--no-seed` escape hatch forces the cold path unconditionally.

## Security model (D-004)

- **Corestore seed** is **already epoch-ciphertext by construction.**
  `pot-epoch-content-ops.ts` encrypts every pot *content* op under the current pot
  epoch key (exclude-set: only admission/key/policy tags stay plaintext). So a bundled
  corestore seed is **useless bytes until admission delivers the wrapped epoch key** —
  a removed/never-member replicates the ciphertext but cannot read it. This is why
  bundling the substrate in a *public* installer is safe (D-003).
- **Git seed** of the **private** repo has no such intrinsic protection, so it must be
  **encrypted at rest** in the installer, with the key delivered **post-admission**
  (`SeedKeyRef.via: "seed-key-op"` — a dedicated admission content-op wrapped to the
  member's device key, mirroring the epoch-key distribution in
  `pot-epoch-key-provider.ts`). A public installer must never leak the codebase.

## Resolved open questions

**Q-1 — installer size budget (full vs shallow git history).** *Decide by measurement
in P-006.* The git `.git` is ~6.2 GB; a full-history bundle roughly doubles installer
weight, a `--depth`-shallow bundle is far smaller but loses history (and a later
unshallow is a big fetch). **Recommendation:** ship a **shallow** git seed by default
(most first-boot value is a working tree + recent history) with the corestore seed
full; expose depth as a cutter knob; confirm against real numbers in P-006. Not
load-bearing for the design — the manifest is depth-agnostic.

**Q-2 — git-seed encryption envelope.** `xchacha20poly1305` over the bundle bytes,
key = a per-release seed key wrapped to each admitted member's device key via a
`seed-key` admission content-op (same sealing primitive as `unwrapEpochKey`). Decrypt
happens **after** admission, immediately before the git restore's fetch step. The
corestore seed needs no extra envelope (epoch-ciphertext already).

**Q-3 — cross-core cut skew.** **Harmless.** Each core is individually consistent at
its recorded length, and the LWW read-merge + idempotent `INSERT … ON CONFLICT`
projections already reconcile arbitrary interleavings (the exact property
`backfill-local-state.ts` relies on). A seed cut with cores at slightly different
lengths is indistinguishable from a peer that replicated them in a different order; the
delta catch-up fills each core forward independently. No global snapshot barrier needed.

**Q-4 — pot epoch read-cut for new members (the one real policy fork).** Content is
encrypted per-epoch; a member decrypts an epoch only if it **holds that epoch's wrapped
key** (`pot-epoch-key-provider.ts`, fail-closed). The read cut-off
(`pot-epoch-boundary.ts`) is designed to stop **REMOVED** members from reading
*future* epochs — it says nothing about whether a **newly-admitted, trusted** member
receives **past-epoch** keys. So seeded history that predates an epoch boundary is
decryptable by a new member **iff** the owner's admission wraps the *past* epoch keys
for them.

- If the dogfood pot has had **no boundary bumps** (members added, never removed —
  the expected canonical-pot case), all content is under one epoch and a newly-admitted
  member's single wrapped key decrypts the entire seed. **Seeded history just works.**
- If boundaries exist, seeded pre-boundary content is dead ciphertext to a
  current-epoch-only member — which is **still correct and still delta-efficient** (they
  catch up live from the boundary forward).

**RATIFIED (owner, 2026-07-04, D-009) — and, on grounding the code, already the
guaranteed default, so no new key-distribution code is needed.** The owner-side
`grantEpochKeysToMembers` (`pot-epoch-boundary-wiring.ts`) **already wraps EVERY
epoch key `[0..current]` to a newly-admitted member**, unconditionally — a documented
*correctness* property ("Why [0..current], not current-only"), because content is
encrypted once per epoch and never re-encrypted, so a current-epoch-only joiner could
read *zero* pre-join content. Restricting new members to the current epoch is explicitly
called out there as a *deferred* forward-secrecy policy that nobody has built. So a
newly-admitted member holds keys for every epoch the seed spans, and the corestore
seed's epoch-ciphertext decrypts for free — and where a key hasn't arrived yet, the
existing **decrypt-gate defers the op and drains it on key arrival** (`pot-epoch-op-gate.ts`),
so a seeded op for a not-yet-keyed epoch is never lost. P-005b therefore reduces to a
**named regression tripwire** (`seed-past-epoch-key-guarantee.test.ts`) that locks the
`[0..current]` grant as a seed dependency: if the deferred forward-secrecy policy is ever
implemented, that test fails and forces wiring the `manifest.cutAtEpoch` gate (defer a
store to the cold path when the member lacks its epoch key) *first*. `manifest.cutAtEpoch`
is carried for exactly that future guard.

## Cold path stays first-class (D-007)

`--no-seed` + restore-failure fallback + a **scheduled cold-join canary** (a periodic
fresh cold join with no seed) keep the full cold path exercised, so the dogfood's
worst-case coverage is preserved even though most installs take the seeded fast path.

## What P-002…P-011 build against this

- **P-002** implements the `libs/generic/seed-bundle` contract above.
- **P-003/P-004** implement the two `SeedProvider`s (corestore, git) with two-peer /
  fixture integration tests proving **delta-only** transfer after restore.
- **P-005** lands the git-seed encryption + the Q-4 pot-policy nod.
- **P-006** builds the release-time cutter + Tauri bundled-resource embedding and
  **measures** Q-1.
- **P-007** wires restore-before-join into `bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts` (unchanged
  join after).
- **P-008** the fallback + canary. **P-009** a second (test-rig) consumer to prove
  genericity. **P-010** the fresh-install E2E (cold vs seeded, delta-only assertion +
  full-join-still-exercised assertion). **P-011** the FLAG (default ON) + docs.
